prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild the print as a self-contained, animated low-poly wallpaper.

[action] Created [scene/index.html](./scene/index.html). I chose a nearly fixed viewpoint so the curling breaker continues to frame Mount Fuji as the water moves. All geometry, color, and paper grain are generated in code.

[result] Opened the file directly in Edge and inspected the [rendered scene](./tmp/review.jpg). Browser checks returned `Distinct animated frames: true` and `Paused frame stable: true`. I closed the review browsers. Automatic review blocked deletion of temporary review files.

[next] Open the HTML directly to use the wallpaper. [result.json](./result.json) records **3 boats** and **Mount Fuji**. I counted one boat beneath the left breaker, one crossing the mountain’s base, and one in the foreground, then checked all three positions against the render.
